what: Video to GIF turns a short part of a video into an animated GIF that plays and loops by itself in chats, emails, documents and web pages. You choose where the GIF starts, how long it lasts, how wide it is and how smooth it plays.

GIFs can only show 256 colours, so simple converters often look grainy. This tool first works out the best palette of colours for your exact clip and then maps every frame onto it, which gives clean, bright GIFs at a sensible file size.
It all runs in your browser with a built-in copy of FFmpeg. Your video is never uploaded.
uses: Turn a funny moment from your own video into a GIF to send in group chats.
Make a short looping demo of an app, a recipe step or a craft for a blog post or a help page.
A 3-second loop of a product turning around catches the eye without needing a video player.
GIFs play inline in GitHub, Jira, Notion and many other tools, so a short screen capture explains a problem fast.
Most email apps cannot play video but do show GIFs. Use a small GIF to add movement to an email.
tutorial: Click "Click or drop a video here" or drag a video onto it. MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV and AVI files work. The first time, the video engine (about 32 MB) downloads with a progress message.
Play the video in the preview and pause where the GIF should begin, then press "Start the GIF here". Or type the time in "Start time", like 0:12.5 or 12.5.

Type the number of seconds in "Length (seconds, max 20)". A note under the settings shows the GIF's size in pixels, the number of frames and the length. Press "Play this part" to watch exactly what will become the GIF.

In "Frames per second" choose 5 to 25; 12 is smooth enough for most clips. In "Width" choose from 240 to 800 px; the height follows automatically. Smaller width and fewer frames make a much smaller file.
"Colours" sets the palette size: 256 looks best, 64 is a bit smaller. "Playback" lets the GIF loop forever or play once and stop.
Click "Make GIF". A progress bar shows the work, and Cancel stops it. When it is done the GIF appears below so you can check it, with its file size in the message.
Click "Download GIF". The file is named after your video, for example holiday.gif.
features: A two-step palette is built for every clip, so colours stay rich and smooth.
Use the player and Start the GIF here, or type a time to the tenth of a second.
Choose the width, frame rate, length and number of colours to balance quality and file size.
Make an endless loop or a GIF that stops after one play.
See the finished GIF on the page before you download it.
Works entirely in your browser, so your video stays private.

example.title: Worked example: a GIF of a dog catching a ball
example.text: Your 45-second phone video shows the catch at about 0:21. You drop it in, pause the player at 0:20.5 and press Start the GIF here, then type 3 in Length. With 12 frames per second and a width of 480 px, the note says GIF: 480 × 270 px, 36 frames, 0:03.0 long. You click Make GIF and a few seconds later the looping GIF appears, about 1 MB in size. You click Download GIF and send dog.gif to your friends.

tips: Keep GIFs short: 2 to 5 seconds is ideal, and every extra second adds to the file size.
For chat apps, 320 or 480 px wide at 10 to 12 frames per second is plenty.
Busy scenes with lots of detail make bigger GIFs than simple ones. Lower the width if the file is too large.
Need sound? GIFs cannot have any. Make a short MP4 clip with the Video Trimmer instead.
Use Play once for GIFs that end on a result, like a finished drawing, so it stays on the final frame.
problems: The GIF is too big to send
Lower the width to 320 or 240 px, set frames per second to 8 to 10, and shorten the length. Each of these cuts the file size a lot.
It says the length is over 20 seconds
Long GIFs become huge and can crash the browser, so the limit is 20 seconds. Use the Video Trimmer to make a short MP4 instead.
The GIF is shorter than I asked
Your start time was close to the end of the video, so the GIF stops where the video ends.
Your browser cannot play this video format. Type the start time instead; making the GIF still works.
The video could not be read
The file may be damaged or not a real video. Try playing it in another app first, or convert it to MP4 with the Video Converter.
